name: WXC round-trip through its own pair returns more than it costs
summary: Inside a Moolah WBNB flash loan the attacker bought 7.4963e25 WXC out of the WXC/WBNB pair and sold the same amount straight back through the router for a 37.5 WBNB profit, because WXC's fee-on-transfer handling leaves the pair short of the balance it accounts for.

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

lastCodeChange.description: Legacy basis: latest of 11 pre-incident Upgraded event(s).

limitations: Target identity and code history came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/wxc-token.json; no semantic revalidation was inherited.

sources.note: onchain review: victim 0x8087720eeea59f9f04787065447d52150c09643e created 2025-08-01T03:59:53Z by 0x5ad3db2dca84d949edf5d769f48be9f548bbb358, which is not the attack-tx sender 0x476954c752a6ee04b68382c97f7560040eda7309; 11 EIP-1967 Upgraded events on the victim before the incident; code age measured from last of 11 upgrade events (onchain). 37.5 WBNB x $824.7/BNB at the incident timestamp 1754881158 (DefiLlama coingecko:binancecoin) = $30,926. The WXC proxy had been upgraded 2,651 seconds (44 minutes) before the incident, which is where the code age is measured from.
